how.title: How it works
how.intro: Routeur Voile computes several possible routes for your boat from the game's weather and 31 variants of that weather. Here is where the data comes from, when it updates and how the advice is built.
how.data.title: The data
how.data.gfs: Game weather: NOAA GFS model at 0.25°, the one Virtual Regatta uses. Wind at 10 m, hourly up to 5 days.
how.data.gefs: 31 scenarios: NOAA GEFS at 0.5°, the same forecast run 31 times with small changes in its starting point, every 3 hours.
how.data.polar: Boat polar: the game's Class40 polar (community copy dated 2024-07-02). It gives the speed for each wind strength and angle for each of the 7 sails, with the foil and hull bonuses and manoeuvre times.
how.data.course: Course: the official 2026 sailing instructions (amendments 1 and 2). Start line, Fréhel gate, Guadeloupe marks, finish line and 22 forbidden zones.
how.data.geo: Coastline and depths: Natural Earth (1:10 million scale), public domain.
how.fresh.title: When the weather updates
how.fresh.runs: NOAA publishes a new forecast four times a day: the 00, 06, 12 and 18 UTC runs. Each run becomes available about 4 to 5 hours later.
how.fresh.cache: The site downloads each run once and keeps it. A computation started after an update therefore uses the latest weather automatically. The run in use and the time of the next update are shown in "Legend and sources".
how.fresh.when: Good habit: recompute after 05, 11, 17 and 23 UTC.
how.fresh.now: For now the map shows an example: the wind is real (31/10, 06 UTC run) but the options and their probabilities are made up until the routing engine is wired in.
how.route.title: How a route is computed
how.route.intro: The router uses the isochrone method, the one professional routers use:
how.route.1: Start from your position, at the current time.
how.route.3: For each heading, read the forecast wind at that place and time, pick the fastest sail from the polar, and sail for 1 hour (3 hours beyond 24 h).
how.route.4: A tack, a gybe or a sail change costs time: about 1 to 2 minutes lost depending on the wind, from the game's settings.
how.route.5: Any track that crosses the coast or a forbidden zone is dropped.
how.route.6: Among the thousands of points, keep the most advanced one in each direction. This line of points reachable at the same time is called an isochrone.
how.route.7: Start again from that line, hour after hour, until the finish or 5 days.
how.route.8: Finally walk back from the most advanced point: that is the route, with heading, sail and speed at each step.
how.options.title: From scenarios to options
how.options.why: A single forecast can be wrong. So a route is computed for each of the 31 GEFS scenarios, then routes that pass the same place at +24 h and +48 h are grouped. Each group becomes an option, for example "West option".
how.options.probability: An option's probability is the share of scenarios whose best route belongs to that group: 17 scenarios out of 31 give 55%. The route computed with the game's exact weather carries the "Game weather" badge.
how.options.confidence: The confidence of a route-plan step is the share of the option's scenarios that pass through the target area at that time. It drops over time, as the weather gets less certain.
how.options.now: "Set this now" gives the heading, sail, wind and speed at the very start of the selected option. At the start, several options often share the same settings while they follow the same path.
how.limits.title: What the tool does not do
how.limits.advice: It does not play for you: you enter your orders in the game yourself.
how.limits.game: The game may differ slightly: Virtual Regatta does not publish its coastline, its exact penalties or its skipper energy model.
how.limits.polar: The polar is a community copy, not yet verified in the game.
how.limits.horizon: Beyond 2 to 3 days the weather gets uncertain: recompute at each new run.
